arabic_blocks: [906] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني سالم بن عبد الله أن عبد الله بن عمر قال أخذ عمر جبة من إستبرق تباع في السوق فأخذها فأتى رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله ابتع هذه تجمل بها للعيد والوفود، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ إنما هذه لباس من لا خلاق له فلبث عمر ما شاء الله أن يلبث ثم أرسل إليه رسول الله ﷺ بجبة ديباج فأقبل بها عمر فأتى بها رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: يا رسول الله إنك قلت: إنما هذه لباس من لا خلاق له وأرسلت إلي بهذه الجبة، فقال له رسول الله ﷺ تبيعها أو تصيب بها حاجتك
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri. He said: Salim ibn ‘Abdullah informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar said:

‘Umar took a robe of thick silk that was being sold in the market. He took it and came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, buy this and adorn yourself with it for Eid and for delegations.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘This is only the clothing of one who has no share.’ ‘Umar remained as long as Allah willed him to remain. Then the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, sent him a robe of silk brocade. ‘Umar came with it and brought it to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, you said, “This is only the clothing of one who has no share,” yet you have sent me this robe.’ The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to him, ‘Sell it, or meet your need with it.’

english_blocks: Ahmad related to us. He said: Ibn Wahb related to us. He said: ‘Amr informed us that Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Asadi related to him, from ‘Urwah, from ‘A’ishah. She said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came in to me while two girls were with me, singing the songs of Bu‘ath. He lay down on the bed and turned his face away. Abu Bakr came in and rebuked me, saying, ‘A pipe of Satan in the presence of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace!’ The Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, turned towards him and said, ‘Leave them both.’ When he became inattentive, I signalled to the two of them, and they went out.

It was an Eid day, and the Black people were playing with shields and spears. Either I asked the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, or he said, ‘Would you like to watch?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He stood me behind him, my cheek against his cheek, while he was saying, ‘Carry on, Banu Arfidah!’ When I grew tired, he said, ‘Is that enough for you?’ I said, ‘Yes.’ He said, ‘Then go.’

english_blocks: ‘Uthman related to us. He said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Sha‘bi, from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, addressed us on the day of Adha after the prayer. He said, ‘Whoever prays our prayer and performs our sacrifice has fulfilled the sacrifice. Whoever sacrifices before the prayer has done so before the prayer, and has no sacrifice.’ Abu Burdah ibn Niyar, al-Bara’s maternal uncle, said, ‘Messenger of Allah, I sacrificed my sheep before the prayer. I knew that today was a day of eating and drinking, and I wanted my sheep to be the first thing slaughtered in my house. So I slaughtered my sheep and ate my midday meal before coming to the prayer.’ He said, ‘Your sheep is a sheep for meat.’ He said, ‘Messenger of Allah, we have a young she-goat that is dearer to me than two sheep. Will it suffice for me?’ He said, ‘Yes, but it will not suffice for anyone after you.’

english_blocks: Sa‘id ibn Abi Maryam related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Ja‘far related to us. He said: Zayd informed me, from ‘Iyad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri. He said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would go out on the day of Fitr and Adha to the prayer ground. The first thing he began with was the prayer. Then he would turn and stand facing the people, while they remained seated in their rows. He would admonish them, counsel them and give them instructions. If he wished to dispatch a force, he dispatched it, or to order something, he ordered it. Then he would leave.

Abu Sa‘id said: The people continued in this way until I went out with Marwan, who was the governor of Madinah, on Adha or Fitr. When we reached the prayer ground, there was a pulpit built by Kathir ibn al-Salt. Marwan wanted to climb it before praying. I pulled at his garment, and he pulled me. He went up and delivered the sermon before the prayer. I said to him, ‘By Allah, you have changed things.’ He said, ‘Abu Sa‘id, what you know has gone.’ I said, ‘By Allah, what I know is better than what I do not know.’ He said, ‘The people would not remain seated for us after the prayer, so I placed it before the prayer.’

english_blocks: Abu Ma‘mar related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Hafsah bint Sirin. She said:

We used to prevent our girls from going out on the day of Eid. A woman came and stayed at the palace of Banu Khalaf. I went to her, and she related that her sister’s husband had gone on twelve expeditions with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and her sister was with him on six expeditions. She said, ‘We used to tend the sick and treat the wounded.’ She said, ‘Messenger of Allah, is there any blame on one of us if she has no outer garment and does not go out?’ He said, ‘Let her companion cover her with her outer garment, and let them witness the good and the supplication of the believers.’ Hafsah said: When Umm ‘Atiyyah arrived, I went to her and asked her, ‘Did you hear about such-and-such?’ She said, ‘Yes, may my father be ransomed for him.’
She seldom mentioned the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, without saying, ‘May my father be ransomed for him.’
He said, ‘Let the young women in seclusion go out’—or he said, ‘The young women and the women in seclusion’—
Ayyub was uncertain.

‘And the menstruating women.
